A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HUMORCHAIN study. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, added, and removed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original human caption evaluations, automated metrics, discriminator training results, and qualitative examples in Sections 4–5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds discriminator ablations, robustness experiments, theory-coverage analysis, failure cases, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The four reasoning strategies, safety filtering, discriminator architecture, training approach, and appendix prompts are retained. Section 3.2.3 newly documents a five-retry limit and top-rated-candidate fallback; v1 specifies no conflicting policy, so this establishes additional implementation documentation rather than a demonstrated change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Meme-Image-No-Text, Oogiri-GO, and OxfordTVG-HIC for humorous captioning and discriminator development/evaluation. The additional analyses use retained coverage; subsampling, prompt variations, and another backbone do not establish a new dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds comparator J, HUMORCHAIN without the discriminator and retry loop, with comparisons against I, A, F, CLoT, and OxfordTVG-HIC captions. Existing generation baselines and the larger-model discriminator comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands the evaluation design: five additional 300-sample pairwise comparisons involving J, 100-sample prompt and Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct experiments, theory analysis on 100 OxfordTVG-HIC samples, strategy analysis on 25% of generated captions, and 100-sample token-cost measurement. Original dataset splits, training parameters, and annotation rules are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's strategy/classifier comparisons and qualitative examples, v2 adds a direct discriminator-and-retry ablation, prompt sensitivity and backbone-transfer tests, theory applicability and strategy-distribution analyses, three failure cases in Figure 4, and computational-cost analysis. Appendix robustness discussion consequently gains experimental support.

E5.justification: v2 removes the entire p-value column from Table 3, eliminating the reported significance results for all original pairwise comparisons without replacement uncertainty estimates. Significance-testing language remains. Appendix B adds an unsupported-by-details statement of no significant strategy–quality correlation; repeated-run reporting does not expand, and discriminator seed 3407 is unchanged.

E6.justification: Original matched pairwise rates and Tables 4–5 and 7–8 remain unchanged. New results include J's win rates of 0.850 against A and 0.830 against F, I's 0.745 against J, robustness outcomes, 86% theory applicability, and token-cost measurements. Table 6 removes accuracy, recall, and F1 results while retaining the same precision values.

T1.justification: The conceptual humor theories and their mappings to generation strategies are retained. Neither version provides formal mathematical theory or proofs that are revised; v2's theory-validation appendix adds empirical analysis rather than mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: theory-guided structured generation, a human-preference discriminator and feedback loop, a dataset exceeding 5,000 pairs, and superior humor performance. The new experiments support these retained claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking failures to inadequate visual descriptions and weak visual–humor connections, and discusses balancing theory coverage against computational complexity. It also interprets new experiments as evidence of prompt stability and backbone independence and states that human annotation mitigates prompt-induced bias. Existing cultural and subjective limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies GPT-5-2025-08-07, documents the five-retry limit and top-rated fallback, and explains token-cost accounting that excludes the discriminator. The detailed prompts, LoRA/classifier settings, generation parameters, and training/validation counts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Qwen3-VL technical-report reference. Section 2.1 also explicitly distinguishes OxfordTVG-HIC's use of humor theories for evaluation from HUMORCHAIN's integration into generation. The broader related-work coverage and positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical and terminology corrections, adds an equal-contribution author footnote, and inserts the retry subsection and additional appendix sections. Existing appendices are renumbered around these additions; the main narrative structure and extensive prompt text remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds failure-case Figure 4 and cost Table 10, corrects Figure 1's duplicated contrast-irony label to absurdity, and enlarges/repositions existing qualitative panels. Tables 1–2 exchange numbering and placement, comparison tables gain J, Table 3 loses its p-value column, and Table 6 becomes precision-only. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: The direct I-versus-J ablation supplies evidence about the discriminator and retry loop beyond v1's indirect precision-based assessment. Robustness tests, failure cases, cost measurements, and clearer implementation details improve assessment of the framework's contribution and practical limits. These gains are tempered by removing pairwise p-values and discriminator accuracy/recall/F1 reporting while retaining strong superiority language, yielding a limited net improvement.
